[INBO 2021 — question paper]
7. (1 point) „Mostly male‟ hypothesis of Michael and Frohlich states that bisexual flower
organization derives more from the male structures of ancestral gymnosperms than from
female structures. From which of the following facts is this hypothesis derived?
a. Male cones of certain pteridophytes and gymnosperms resemble primitive flowers like lotus.
b. Genes for flower development in angiosperms and microsporophyll development in
gymnosperms are closely related.
c. Position of flowers resembles that of male cones.
d. All the above.

[CBSE Class XII Biology, sample question paper, 2026-27]
1. A researcher observes that in a particular flowering plant, the pistil matures 1
several days before the stamens in all flowers of the plant. What is the most
significant consequence of this timing difference?
A. It guarantees self-pollination
B. It promotes autogamy
C. It ensures cross-pollination
D. It leads to geitonogamy

[INBO 2011 — question paper]
48. (2 points) Floral diagrams are used to graphically represent a flower. Given
below is a floral diagram of a flower:
Which of the following properties does it convey?
1. Presence of three sepals
2. Having a tricarpellary syncarpous ovary
3. Presence of three fertile stamens
4. Presence of a bract
a. Only 1, 3 and 4
b. Only 1, 2 and 4
c. Only 2 and 3
d. Only 2
Choose from the options and put a tick mark (√) in the appropriate box.
a. b. c. d.

[CBSE Class XII Biology, marking scheme, 2022-23]
23. (a) Corn: Wind. Numerous flowers are packed in an inflorescence; the 3
tassels seen in the corn cob are the stigma and style which wave in the
wind to trap pollen grains.
(b) Water hyacinth: Insects or wind. In water hyacinth the flowers emerge
above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind as in
most of the land plants.
(c) Vallisneria: Water, In Vallisneria - the female flower reaches the surface
of water by the long stalk and the male flowers or pollen grains are
released onto the surface of water. They are carried passively by water
currents; some of them eventually reach the female flowers and the
stigma.
(½ x 6 =3 Marks)
